fixes.explanation: Wood sounds sturdy, I'll give you that. But the text says, “So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.” (Genesis 11:3) Wood never makes the list. These folks baked bricks and let them do the job of stone. I spent years in a junk drawer next to a twist tie, so believe me, I know a thing or two about building with whatever's lying around. Nobody ever built a tower out of a twist tie, though. We tried in my head.

I see why you'd pick it, since the tower has been the talk of the whole passage. But the LORD says, “Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.” (Genesis 11:7) He doesn't say He'll bring the tower down. He goes after their speech. Picture it: one person says "pass the tar," and the person next to them hears something that sounds like "my cousin's a tuba." That's a whole different workday!

Not quite, baker. The text says, “So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.” (Genesis 11:8) The scattering came, and the building stopped. I think a crew that suddenly can't understand each other has a hard time saying "pass the tar." Picture getting a blank stare back!

problems.problem: The explanation is flat, and the drawer line ends on a pleasant sentiment rather than a laugh.
The explanation is generic and purely functional, with no laugh where the language confusion could support one.
The imagined feeling is marked as a guess, but the explanation also invents a foreman and a pile of bricks that the passage does not mention.
